rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a small involuntary movement of the face or a muscle.

example.english: My finger suddenly had a twitch.
example.traditional: 我隻手指突然抽動咗一下。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zek3 sau2 zi2 dat6 jin4 cau1 dung6 zo2 jat1 haa5

rows.note: Use this when the twitch is more spasmodic or medically described rather than just a slight movement.

example.english: The patient's arm kept having a twitch, and the doctor said it needed an immediate examination.
example.traditional: 病人嘅手臂持續抽搐，醫生話要即刻檢查。
example.jyutping: beng6 jan4 ge3 sau2 bei3 ci4 zuk6 cau1 cuk1 ji1 sang1 waa6 jiu3 zik1 hak1 gim2 caa4

rows.note: Use this specifically for an involuntary twitch of the eyelid.

example.english: I’ve had an eyelid twitch all day, and it’s making me uncomfortable.
example.traditional: 我今日成日眼皮跳，搞到我好唔舒服。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 seng4 jat6 ngaan5 pei4 tiu3 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 hou2 m4 syu1 fuk6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for an involuntary small twitch of a body part or muscle.

example.english: I have a twitch in my eye today.

rows.note: Use this when the jerk is a brief deliberate tug on something, especially a sleeve to get attention.

example.english: Give my sleeve a little twitch and I’ll know you’re calling me.

rows.note: Use this construction when something causes a person or body part to twitch.

example.english: Not getting enough sleep last night made my eye twitch.
example.traditional: 噚晚冇瞓夠，搞到我隻眼抽。
example.jyutping: cam4 maan5 mou5 fan3 gau3 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 zek3 ngaan5 cau1
